sections.heading: Getting Started in 1M Clicks To Escape
paragraphs: The game's public description frames your task as escaping a white room by pressing a large red button one million times. That is the stated objective. We do not have a verified speedrun route, a complete map, or a demonstration that any particular shortcut is required to finish.

Open the experience identified by Roblox Place ID 138666683767450. Before trusting a tip, check whether the game you entered displays the same name and goal. Similar titles can lead to guides that describe unrelated mechanics.

Notice what the game itself displays when you start: a button or interaction prompt, a progress counter if one is present, any gem balance, and upgrade options. These are observation checkpoints, not claims that every device or version uses the same interface.

steps.description: Open the official Roblox experience and compare its title to this guide.

steps.heading: Find the stated objective
steps.description: Look for the large red button mentioned by the public description, and follow the live prompts rather than assumed key bindings.

steps.heading: Observe before spending
steps.description: If progress, gems, or upgrades are shown, record their labels and costs before making a purchase.

sections.heading: The Red Button and the Million-Click Goal
paragraphs: The number 1,000,000 is part of the game premise; it does not tell us the precise number of physical inputs you will need. A counter might react to upgrades, automatic actions, or game modes, but those relationships have not been measured for this guide.

For a reliable first-run note, look at the displayed counter before a short series of actions and again afterward. Write down what changed, what tool or upgrade was equipped, and whether an auto-click feature was enabled. Without a before-and-after observation, avoid claiming a clicks-per-second rate.
If the game offers a way to track a run, use its visible readout. Do not confuse a promotional number in an article with a measurement inside your actual session.

subsections.heading: What to record
paragraphs: Record the progress value before and after a short interval, any visible action prompt, and whether an upgrade was active. These values are yours to measure and are not prefilled here.

subsections.heading: What this guide does not assume
paragraphs: We do not claim a verified macro, a hidden input trick, a guaranteed completion time, or a specific ending after the counter reaches its target.

sections.heading: Gems and Upgrades: Make a Decision with Evidence
paragraphs: The description says players earn gems and spend them on upgrades. The current costs, exact modifiers, shop names, and acquisition rates have not been independently validated. Therefore a fixed 'best upgrades' ranking would be misleading.

If you see an upgrade in the game, compare its displayed price with your available gems and read the effect before purchasing. After buying it, observe how the actual progress counter behaves. Keep notes instead of assuming a third-party efficiency claim is accurate for the current version.

An effective comparison needs actual data: cost, displayed description, progress before, progress after, and the amount of time observed. The following worksheet fields are intentionally blank because we do not have real in-game measurements.

sections.heading: Friends and the Group Auto Clicker
paragraphs: The public description mentions playing with up to three friends and a free auto clicker associated with joining the developer's Roblox group. That is a published promotional claim, not a tested guarantee that a particular benefit is active in all builds.

Check the current Roblox experience and its official group information before joining anything. Avoid third-party downloads, executables, or sites promising auto-clickers; they are not required by this guide and can introduce account security risks.
If you are playing with others, compare your progress in the actual game rather than assuming the group size changes click counts or gem rewards. No co-op multiplier is established in our research.

sections.heading: Next Steps and Limits
paragraphs: If you want to check a published code, use the Codes page, which labels CHAPTER2 as developer-listed rather than redeem-tested. If you are looking for the current Chapter 2 status, read the dated Chapter 2 page; it is not a full walkthrough of an untested update.
